tierWindow.goal: Write as a member of your discipline: recognise that academic writing is situated in a discipline, work out its conventions from published writing, and integrate sources with a critical edge so your writing advances your own argument.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Analysis, evaluation and independent application (analyse, appraise, adapt, integrate, articulate).
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Open, discipline-situated judgements; conventions that vary by field and genre, with no single right answer.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; the learner brings their own discipline and texts; feedback prompts refinement rather than confirming a single answer.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner is a later-stage student who can already work through the writing process and get a draft structured and clear. What is new is treating writing as the practice of a discipline: recognising, learning and adopting the conventions of their own field, and writing with a critical edge. Teach from that capable starting point, not from first principles.

subThemes.label: Academic writing is not monolithic: it is situated in, and shaped by, the discipline you write in

Integrating academic sources with the 'voices' technique so they serve your own argument

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, that writing is situated in your discipline: why there is no single academic writing, and how fields differ. Second, reading your discipline as a writer: how to work out a field's conventions from the writing already published in it. Third, a critical edge: integrating sources so they serve your own argument, and signalling where you are being critical. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course is about writing as a member of your discipline. By now you can work through the writing process and get a draft structured and clear. The step this course takes is different. It treats academic writing not as one universal skill but as a practice shaped by the field you write in.

By the end you will be able to explain how writing conventions vary across disciplines and characterise your own, appraise published writing to work out its conventions, and integrate sources with a critical edge so that your writing advances an argument of your own.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: explain how conventions vary and characterise your own, appraise published writing to work out its conventions, integrate sources with a critical edge.

practiceConnection.academic: Writing within your discipline is what the later stages of a degree reward, and what professional and research writing demand. Every essay, report, dissertation chapter and journal submission is judged partly on whether it reads like the work of someone inside the field. The conventions you learn to recognise and adopt here are the ones your markers already use, mostly without naming them.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: This is the most advanced course in the Academic Writing pathway. If any foundations felt shaky, the introductory course on the writing process and the intermediate course on argument, structure and sources sit beneath it. Going wider, the same disciplinary habits underpin Criticality, Researching and Reflective Practice, where you put writing within your discipline to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Writing within your discipline is no longer a vague aim: it is something you can recognise, learn and do. You can explain why there is no single academic writing, and characterise the conventions of your own field. You can appraise published work as a writer to work those conventions out. And you can integrate sources with a critical edge, using the 'voices' technique and the language of criticality so that your writing advances an argument of your own. Look back at the confidence check to see how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, writing as a member of your discipline is something you practise in every assignment. Each time you match a field's conventions, work them out from what you read, or use a source to serve your own argument, you are doing the work this course named. It is also what research and professional writing reward: the ability to write as an insider, with judgement that is visibly your own.
